t: You're looking at Savoy Place, a large red brick building on the north bank of the Thames, with the Victoria Embankment in front of it. Savoy Hill and Savoy Street run up its sides to the Strand. The Savoy Hotel and Waterloo Bridge are close by, and there are commanding views across to the South Bank and the London Eye. The name goes back to Peter II, Count of Savoy, nicknamed the Little Charlemagne. In 1243 he was granted land by the Thames on the Strand, and the Savoy name has stayed here ever since.
